output.brief:
The Kestria buffering is almost certainly caused by the smart-TV app 5.2 release, not the move to Tessaline. In the playback data from 12–25 October, smart-TV 5.2 viewers sit at about 5.9% rebuffering, while every other app and device on the same Tessaline CDN is at 0.6–0.7%, the same as before the move. The pattern holds across all three ISPs. Handball nights show no effect, and the rise began on 9 October, the same day 5.2 went live. Smart-TV 5.2 also starts video more slowly on average (1.5 s against 2.4 s for others), which is inconsistent with a delivery fault. I am fairly confident in this, but the mechanism (the 5.2 adaptive-streaming behaviour) is inferred, not directly observed.

Do not send the SLA notice, withhold fees or move traffic back; that would punish Tessaline for a problem its network is not showing. Do not mute the alert. Next, revert 5.2's adaptive-streaming settings in Kestria to 5.1 and pause the wider 5.2 rollout. Then check whether the cancellations are linked to this, and decide on refunds afterwards. Adding app version to the dashboard is worth doing, though the pipeline work takes about six weeks.
